newsitem.title: FRANCE: Investors take a shine to AGF.
newsitem.headline: Investors take a shine to AGF.

text.p: Shares in insurer AGF rose sharply in heavy trading on the Paris bourse on Thursday as investors re-evaluated the recently privatised company.
Its stock was up 3.60 francs at 151.60 at 1420 GMT in a weaker market. Turnover totalled 1.21 million shares.
Some brokers speculated there may have been a big buy order out for the stock.
"The evolution envisaged at the time of the privatisation was confirmed in the half-year results," said analyst Danny Jacques at Du Bouzet.

The group announced a first-half profit of 723 million francs last month and said it expected to show a full year profit of around twice that amount, compared with a profit of 1.08 billion francs for 1995.
An AGF spokesman said the company began a round of European roadshows on September 23 to discuss its first-half results.
Analyst Sami Gotrane at EIFB said the market had been wary after previous disappointments with privatised companies.
Analysts say AGF's stock has attained its short-term target of around 150 francs and estimate it will climb to between 165 and 175 francs by the end of the year.
